answer: Chromatic Witness Nonce. Each identity must submit a fresh answer whose correctness depends on a hidden per-epoch challenge derived from the prior block's ferrous oxide sensor feed. Answers are checked against a canonical oracle, so a copied response fails the next epoch's nonce. Registering N identities costs N distinct valid computations per epoch, forcing real compute and data access per identity. The ivory ledger records only passing answers, and any repeated prior signal voids the submission.
